discoveries.body: fireguard spawns bare `npx` without a shell, which fails with ENOENT on Windows. DGI-1, DGI-3, DGI-4 and DGI-5 all needed an out-of-repo NODE_OPTIONS preload shim that maps npx to npx.cmd.
discoveries.title: Make fireguard spawn npx portably on Windows

discoveries.body: With core.autocrlf=true, `npm run format:check` fails locally on 4 to 81 files that this epic never touched, because Prettier expects LF. Adding `* text=auto eol=lf` to .gitattributes, or setting Prettier's endOfLine to auto, would make local results match CI.
discoveries.title: Normalize line endings so format:check passes on Windows checkouts

discoveries.body: The site has no dark-theme CSS tokens, so the plan view's dark screenshots needed a throwaway harness override. The ticket asked for light and dark themes using existing tokens.
discoveries.title: Add dark-theme tokens to src/index.css

discoveries.body: The download of Playwright 1.33's bundled Chromium fails here with HTTP 400 from the CDN, so e2e only runs with system Chrome (PW_USE_SYSTEM_CHROME=1). Upgrading Playwright, or documenting the env var, would unblock local e2e.
discoveries.title: Fix the Playwright browser install for e2e on this machine

discoveries.body: fireguard's mutation testing left 2 survivors at src/components/planLayout.ts:90 (operator swapped to +), so a layout test is probably missing for that line. The code is DGI-4's.
discoveries.title: Kill the surviving mutants at planLayout.ts:90

discoveries.body: The live page logs 404s. index.html references /vite.svg, which does not exist in public/, and GitHub Pages serves the /coding-reference deep link through 404.html with HTTP 404. Both predate this epic.
discoveries.title: Remove the live console 404s on Coding Reference

discoveries.body: During capture, one click landed on a different window (a browser report page) because the app was not in the foreground. A small capture helper that checks the foreground window before every click would make screenshot tickets safer.
discoveries.title: Safe desktop-app capture helper with a foreground check

tierFit.note: Planned routine. The low-cost model's attempt was rejected for voice and citations, and the next tier up was accepted. Copy with source citations needs more than routine.
Planned routine. The orchestrator stepped one tier up front for privacy and GUI driving, and the attempt was accepted first try. What was wrong was the environment (macOS), not the level.
Planned multi_step; accepted first try. The layout defect slipped through review (see wentPoorly), which is a review gap rather than a tier problem.
Planned multi_step; one attempt. The person stopped the first worker after Phase A, and a replacement finished Phase B under the same claim.

wentPoorly: DGI-1's first attempt, on the low-cost model, pasted README sentences instead of writing in first person, and cited wrong source lines. It was rejected and redone one tier up.

DGI-5 was accepted with a broken card structure: the plan section sat outside the card, its heading was nearly invisible, there was no gap before the next card, and the graph was clipped. Neither the e2e spec nor the orchestrator's review checked visual card structure. The person found it.

DGI-2 required a macos-desktop-gui environment, which did not match this Windows host. The question to the person went unanswered for a while, and the ticket idled until it fell back to capturing the Windows app.
The remote epic branch name was already taken by an unrelated October implementation, so publishing needed a new branch name and a decision from the person.
Local tooling on Windows got in the way: autocrlf breaks format:check, fireguard cannot spawn npx, and Playwright's Chromium download fails, so every worker needed workarounds.

Orchestrator process slips: the host could not actually set the reasoning effort (every model was registered as medium); discovering command schemas through the CLI was trial and error; and two placeholder report revisions were submitted by accident while probing the report schema. This revision supersedes them.
wentWell: The dependency graph let DGI-1, DGI-2 and DGI-3 run in parallel, and they joined cleanly in DGI-5. The row check passed at every row.
The allowlist exporter and its poisoned fixture gave strong evidence for the privacy and determinism criteria.
Checking the copy against its sources caught DGI-1's pasted README sentences and wrong citations before acceptance.
The person's hands-on preview caught a layout defect the tests missed, and it was fixed inside the same PR before merge.

risks: The live plan view statuses lag: they reflect the committed .darkmechanicus/ state (all Backlog) until the person commits the final state and it deploys.
The plan-graph screenshot and its alt text are a point-in-time snapshot (DGI-2 running), so they will not match the live plan view's statuses.

The remote branch epic/dark-mechanicus-showcase still holds an unrelated October implementation (418ea86). The shipped work came from epic/dark-mechanicus-showcase-run1. Delete or archive the old branch to avoid confusion.
content.summary: Sprint 1 (the only sprint) delivered the Dark Mechanicus showcase on Coding Reference. DGI-1 to DGI-6 are all accepted. PR #12 was squash-merged to main as 617f4d5, and the Pages deploy (run 41565747679) succeeded. At desktop width and 375px, the live page shows one Dark Mechanicus card: first-person copy with links, two privacy-checked app screenshots, and a read-only plan view. The plan view is generated at build time from the committed .darkmechanicus/ records through an allowlist exporter. The person approved the copy, placement, screenshots and allowlist, and gave the merge go-ahead in chat. Known limitation: the live plan view shows statuses as of the committed records (all Backlog) until the person commits the final .darkmechanicus/ state.
